South hero also opened directly. Fixed target/original opened directly; compared with initial four-view original evidence. Six-placement repeated context inspected at 128 logical pixels per cell.
inspectionMethod.contactSheetParity: Independently reconstructed all six light/gray/dark logical/enlarged sheets from exact published frames and verified identical RGBA. four-view-sheet.png is byte-identical to gray-enlarged.png; heroes, atlases and frames are byte-identical for each facing. Independently verified every published frame equals whole-frame LANCZOS scaling of its corresponding actual native capture.
inspectionMethod.independence: Same judge that defined frozen criteria. Initial inspection preceded editor proposals. No editor ratings used. Only selected round04 reviewed; no candidate/source/production bytes changed.

observations.evidence: Compared with the original four long rigid columns, the selected model gives the broad dominant crown a more worn silhouette, variable sloping shoulder bands, and six overlapping stone masses at distinct heights. Secondary stones wrap the rear as well as the front, so N/E/S/W all retain a deliberate broad base and a clear dominant mass. Rounded exposed crown and shoulder edges are visible at logical size and are real native volume in replay. The upright crag identity remains readable without needle peaks or thin decorative fins.

Broad native facets and restrained triangular fracture planes break up the lower and side masses, especially the S front boulder, E right/front cluster and W main face. Their changes in plane and tone support the modeled stone instead of adding bright painted crack lines. Large quiet faces remain, especially on the dominant S crown, but the silhouette, edge treatment and supporting fractures now provide sufficient stone structure at intended size.

The cobalt/blue identity survives. Crowns receive broad blue/cyan highlights with soft transitions into sides; lower faces retain blue midtones instead of the original near-black panels. Shoulder intersections remain separated on the dark background. The four views share a balanced matte finish without a left/right world light preference, glossy streaks, luminous seams, or a ground shadow. Highlights keep colored surfaces and visible edge volume rather than white/cyan clipped bands.

All four actual facings are clean on light/gray/dark at logical size and enlarged: no material black dead spots, unintended holes or floating shards, alpha halos, broken corners, frame clipping, or muddy black wedges between masses. Flat stone faces remain distinct from the softened bevels. Low contrast internal facets simplify at logical size while the mass hierarchy and worn edges remain legible.

The six-placement preview at the declared 128-pixel cell pitch shows broad cell coverage, grounded scale, stable roots and distinct neighboring crowns. The object repeats visibly as any isolated prop would, but rotated sides vary the silhouette. No directional baked ground shadow appears. No connector/seam behavior is invented for this isolated boulder.

The change is a useful native remodeling of construction, contours and edge volume rather than only a material repaint. Its six stone masses differ from the old four-part source and the target arrangement; those differences preserve role and the frozen technical envelope and are acceptable under modelingPolicy version2.

remainingDifferences: The target has stronger pale-cyan rim accents, more painted surface variation and more dramatic individual fracture outlines. The native candidate uses quieter blue highlights and restrained facets; its readable matte stone finish meets the selected style without reproducing target halo/outline artifacts.

The target silhouette is broader and more intricately staggered on its different canvas. The approved native result keeps the actual one-cell/2.325-unit envelope and source registration; exact target proportion, part count and paint placement are not required.

The dominant crown retains relatively large quiet planes. This is acceptable at game size because its worn edge volume, uneven shoulders and lower stone grouping now supply the required depth and natural crag hierarchy.

independentNativeInspection.method: Fresh Blender5.2.2 background process loaded the exact sealed .blend. Judge-owned inspection measured geometry and actual matrices, inspected scene/material/resources/lights, and replayed all four facings using an independent implementation of the source .42 square-footing formula. No candidate recipe import or .blend save.

cameraRegistration.projection: 35-degree upper orthographic + .42-unit native square footing applied after facing rotation

geometryRootAndLayout.atlas: Four separate 1x1 full-frame atlases; each rect [0,0,384,1024]
geometryRootAndLayout.topology: Six closed native meshes; independent bmesh check found zero non-manifold edges, loose vertices or degenerate faces.

nativeClosureAndLighting.lightRig: One centered broad overhead and eight equal 34W/size5 fills at symmetric positions around the object; actual saved light matrices inspected. No receiver plane. Four node-based matte stone materials use world height only, not camera/view direction.
nativeClosureAndLighting.declaredClosure: Saved native .blend is self-contained. Packet binds exact recipe/input JSON resources and retained closed relocated four-view replay evidence. Independent judge replay also reproduced all four exact RGBA frames with no external assets.

technicalEvidence.limits: Approval concerns this exact boulder-underwater round04 packet. It is not approval of sibling objects, an exact reproduction of the target painting, or a production/publishing action. This static isolated prop requires no modular connector tests, rig/motion playback or GPU stress scene.
